topic.title: Programming Fundamentals
topic.description: Loops, conditionals, basic logic, and standard I/O.

questions.title: Switch Case Fallthrough
questions.explanation: Because there are no break statements, the execution falls through to the subsequent cases after matching case 2.

questions.title: For Loop Scope
questions.explanation: The 'i' inside the loop shadows the outer 'i'. The loop prints 0, 1, 2. After the loop, the outer 'i' (which is still 0) is printed.

questions.title: Comma Operator
questions.explanation: The comma operator evaluates operands left to right and returns the rightmost. So 'a' gets 3. However, the assignment operator '=' has higher precedence than the comma operator, so 'b = 1, 2, 3;' is evaluated as '(b = 1), 2, 3;'. 'b' gets 1.

questions.title: Ternary Operator Associativity
questions.explanation: The ternary operator is right-to-left associative, parsed as 1 ? 2 : (3 ? 4 : 5). Since 1 is true, it returns 2.

questions.title: While Loop Post-decrement
questions.explanation: The condition evaluates x, then decrements it. Iteration 1: 3 (true), x becomes 2, prints 2. Iteration 2: 2 (true), x becomes 1, prints 1. Iteration 3: 1 (true), x becomes 0, prints 0.

questions.title: Short Circuit Evaluation
questions.explanation: a++ evaluates to 0 (false), so the right side (b++) is short-circuited and NOT evaluated. a becomes 1, b remains 1.

questions.title: Static Variables
questions.explanation: Static variable x retains its value between calls. Local variable y is re-initialized to 0 each time.

questions.title: Bitwise Shift
questions.explanation: 1 << 2 shifts bits left by 2 (multiplies by 4), giving 4. 1 >> 1 shifts bits right by 1, giving 0. 4 + 0 = 4.

questions.title: Integer Division
questions.explanation: 5 / 2 is integer division, which truncates to 2. The integer 2 is then implicitly converted to float 2.0.

questions.title: Do-While Loop
questions.explanation: The loop body executes once unconditionally, printing 0. Then i++ evaluates to 0 (which is not < 0), so the loop terminates. i is now 1, so it prints 1.

questions.title: Const Variable Initialization
questions.explanation: A 'const' variable must be initialized at the time of declaration.

questions.title: Static Variable Initialization
questions.explanation: Static local variables are initialized only once and retain their values between function calls.

questions.title: Unsigned Int Underflow
questions.explanation: Decrementing an unsigned int of value 0 causes it to wrap around to its maximum possible value, making it strictly greater than 0.

questions.title: String Concatenation
questions.explanation: The '+' operator is overloaded for std::string to perform string concatenation.

questions.title: Function Overloading Priority
questions.explanation: A float literal (5.5f) is passed. There is no exact float overload, so it promotes to double instead of demoting to int.

questions.title: Sizeof Array Operator
questions.explanation: sizeof(a) returns the total byte size of the array (40). sizeof(a[0]) returns the byte size of one element (4). 40/4 = 10, computing the number of elements.

questions.title: Modulo with Negative Numbers
questions.explanation: In C++, the modulo operator on negative numbers yields a negative remainder (the sign follows the dividend).

questions.title: Floating Point Truncation
questions.explanation: When assigning a floating point to an integer, the decimal portion is truncated (not rounded).

questions.title: Global vs Local Scope
questions.explanation: ::x forces the global scope 'x' (1). The local 'x' in the inner block is 3.

questions.title: Ternary Return Type
questions.explanation: If both branches of the ternary operator are lvalues of the same type, the ternary operator itself returns an lvalue. Therefore, you can assign to it.
